run.question: Compare long-duration battery storage and green hydrogen for grid balancing, focusing on efficiency, duration, infrastructure needs, and uncertainty.
run.title: Grid balancing: batteries vs green hydrogen

report_sections.heading: Bottom line
report_sections.text: Battery storage is better suited to high-efficiency, shorter-duration cycling, while hydrogen becomes more plausible when storage duration is very long and additional conversion losses can be tolerated.

report_sections.heading: Efficiency and operating profile
report_sections.text: The strongest distinction is round-trip efficiency. The evidence in this run consistently places battery storage above the hydrogen pathway, although exact values depend on system configuration and operating assumptions.

report_sections.heading: Duration and infrastructure
report_sections.text: Hydrogen can decouple power capacity from stored energy and may fit seasonal balancing better, but it requires production, storage, transport or on-site handling, and reconversion infrastructure. That makes project-specific infrastructure availability a major determinant.

report_sections.heading: Uncertainty
report_sections.text: Cost comparisons are unusually sensitive to utilization, storage medium, financing, equipment lifetime, and assumptions about future electrolyzer and fuel-cell performance. A single universal break-even duration is not established by the collected evidence.

claims.text: Battery storage has materially higher round-trip efficiency than a power-to-hydrogen-to-power pathway in the compared system examples.
claims.normalized_text: Battery round-trip efficiency exceeds hydrogen round-trip efficiency in compared examples.
claims.verification_summary: Supported by two independent technical sources; qualifiers preserved.

claims.text: Hydrogen storage can support much longer storage durations without requiring battery capacity to scale in the same way as stored energy duration.
claims.normalized_text: Hydrogen storage can decouple stored-energy duration from electrochemical battery capacity scaling.
claims.verification_summary: Supported by system-design and infrastructure evidence.

claims.text: Hydrogen-based grid storage requires additional conversion and storage infrastructure beyond the electrical interconnection itself.
claims.normalized_text: Hydrogen grid storage requires production, storage, and reconversion infrastructure.

claims.text: A modeled battery pathway at 82% round-trip efficiency loses 18 MWh per 100 MWh cycled.
claims.normalized_text: At 82% efficiency, 18 MWh is lost per 100 MWh input.
claims.verification_summary: Deterministic calculation verified from a registered efficiency input.

claims.text: Green hydrogen becomes cheaper than batteries for grid balancing above a single universal storage-duration threshold.
claims.normalized_text: A universal break-even storage duration exists where hydrogen becomes cheaper than batteries.
claims.verification_summary: Conflicting model assumptions; evidence does not justify a universal threshold.

claims.text: Project-specific economics depend strongly on utilization and local infrastructure availability.
claims.normalized_text: Utilization and infrastructure availability materially affect project economics.
claims.verification_summary: Reasoned synthesis from multiple sources; explicitly marked inference.

claims.text: Hydrogen storage has lower siting friction than batteries in all grid contexts.
claims.normalized_text: Hydrogen storage always has lower siting friction than batteries.
claims.verification_summary: No evidence in the run supports the universal qualifier.

source_versions.title: Why hydrogen may matter for seasonal storage
source_versions.lineage_summary: Downstream article citing srcv_002 and srcv_003

evidence_spans.canonical_excerpt: Representative battery systems in the modeled cases operate at substantially higher round-trip efficiency than hydrogen reconversion pathways.
A hydrogen electricity-storage chain requires electrolysis, hydrogen storage, and a reconversion stage in addition to grid interconnection equipment.
Break-even duration shifts materially with utilization, storage-medium cost, financing, and conversion efficiency assumptions.
Some scenarios show hydrogen becoming attractive at longer durations, but the threshold varies widely across published models.

comments.author: Noah Patel
comments.body: The universal-threshold wording looks too strong. The cost model makes this heavily assumption-dependent.

comments.author: Maya Chen
comments.body: Agreed. I kept the report language explicitly project-specific and left the claim disputed for review.
